main_text.p: » Præscientia Dei; si dicatur hominibus: Sive » curratis, sive dormiatis; quod vos præscivit, » qui falli non potest, hoc eritis. Dolosi autem vel » imperiti Medici est, etiam utile medicamentū » sic alligare; ut aut non profit, aut obsit. Sed di- » cendum est: Sic currite, ut comprehendatis; at- » que ut, ipso cursu vestro, ita vos esse præcogni- » tos noveritis, ut legitimè curratis. & si quo a- » lio modo Dei præscietia prædicari potest; ut ho- » minis segnitia repellatur. Quâ de causâ Apostolus pro se vult orare Colossen- » ses; ut manifestet mysterium Christi, ὡς δεῖ » λαλῆσαι. Coloss. 4. v. 4. scil. εἰς οἰκοδομὴν, » ἵνα ἐκ[?] καθαίρεσιν[?] audientiū. 2 Cor. 10. v. 8. & 12. v. 19. & 13. v. 10. Quare mala est consequentia: Non quovis modo proferenda est hæc doctrina: Ergo nullo: imò ei contradicendum, & quidem pertinaciter.

Sed jam propius accedet ad excu- sandum Semipelagianismum, ita per- gens: At illud, dicitis, ferri non potest; quod electionem singulariū personarum ad præscientiam referunt fidei. Potest, inquam, non potest autem, (ne erres) si referant, uti ad causam electionis. Hoc enim jam Se- mipe-

page.notes: Scan shows a printed "»" mark at the start of each quotation line; transcribed as printed. Italic type assumed for the quoted passages (Scripture and Latin quotations); the scan is small, so the exact italic extent is uncertain. Two Greek words are doubtful: "ὡς δεῖ" (accent unclear) and "ἐκ καθαίρεσιν" (the printed form before "καθαίρεσιν" is hard to read, marked [?]). The strips at the far right edge are the neighbouring page and were left out.
